bib.title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 56th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), Long Papers, pages 328-339

question: How can a pretrained language model be fine-tuned for any NLP text classification task without overfitting or catastrophic forgetting, matching CV-style inductive transfer?
hypothesis: Language-model fine-tuning has failed in NLP because of how it was trained, not because of the idea; careful fine-tuning techniques will make it work across tasks.
contributions: ULMFiT, a method for CV-like transfer learning for any NLP task
Discriminative fine-tuning, slanted triangular learning rates and gradual unfreezing to avoid catastrophic forgetting
Significantly outperform the state of the art on six text classification datasets, 18-24% error reduction on the majority
Extremely sample-efficient transfer learning plus an extensive ablation analysis
Release of pretrained models and code

method.summary: Three stages: pretrain an AWD-LSTM language model on Wikitext-103, fine-tune the whole LM on target-task text with discriminative learning rates and slanted triangular schedule, then fine-tune a classifier (LM plus two linear blocks) with gradual unfreezing, concat pooling and BPT3C. One forward and one backward model are trained and their predictions averaged.
method.task: text classification (sentiment, question, topic) via transfer learning from language modelling

datasets.name: TREC-6
datasets.split: 10% of training split off for validation in analyses
datasets.preprocessing: same as Johnson and Zhang 2017 / McCann et al. 2017, plus special tokens for upper-case words, elongation and repetition

datasets.name: IMDb
datasets.split: 10% of training split off for validation in analyses; hyperparameters tuned on IMDb validation set

datasets.name: AG news
datasets.split: 10% of training split off for validation in analyses

models.name: ULMFiT (AWD-LSTM)
models.architecture: AWD-LSTM language model, regular LSTM with no attention or shortcut connections; classifier head of two linear blocks (batch norm, dropout, ReLU then softmax), hidden size 50
models.init_from: pretrained on Wikitext-103, then LM fine-tuned on target data
models.hidden: 1150 hidden activations per layer; embedding size 400
models.context: BPTT batch size of 70 (variable length backpropagation sequences)

other.dropout: 0.4 layers, 0.3 RNN layers, 0.4 input embedding, 0.05 embedding, weight dropout 0.5 on RNN hidden-to-hidden matrix

models.name: CoVe
models.architecture: hypercolumn-style contextualised vectors from MT, 7 million sentence pairs

models.name: DPCNN / CNN / oh-LSTM etc.
models.architecture: Johnson and Zhang text categorization models and others, see Tables 2 and 3

training.objective: language modelling (pretraining and target LM fine-tuning); cross-entropy classification for the classifier stage
training.lr: base 0.004 for LM fine-tuning and 0.01 for classifier; discriminative: last-layer LR chosen by fine-tuning only last layer, lower layers eta_(l-1) = eta_l/2.6
training.lr_schedule: slanted triangular: cut_frac = 0.1, ratio = 32, eta_max = 0.01; linear increase then long linear decay
training.warmup: inferred: the STLR increase phase, first 10% of iterations (cut_frac = 0.1)
training.epochs: tuned per task on validation set; TREC-6 LM fine-tuned 15 epochs; classifier 50 epochs default; ablations fine-tune classifier 50 epochs
training.regularisation: AWD-LSTM dropouts and weight dropout; batch norm and dropout in classifier; gradual unfreezing (one layer per epoch, from last layer)

other.ablation_lrs: Discr uses eta_L = 0.01; chain-thaw uses 0.001 for last layer and 0.0001 for others; 0.001 for all other ablation settings
other.vanilla_LM_ablation: vanilla LM (no dropout) classifier trained only 5 epochs, classifier dropout 0.4 kept
other.concat_pooling: h_c = [h_T, maxpool(H), meanpool(H)] over as many time steps as fit in GPU memory
other.BPT3C: document split into fixed-length batches of size b; model state carried between batches; gradients backpropagated to batches that contributed to final prediction
other.bidirectional: forward and backward LM each pretrained and fine-tuned independently, classifier predictions averaged
other.hyperparameter_tuning: same hyperparameters across tasks, tuned on the IMDb validation set

metrics.name: error rate
metrics.definition: percentage of misclassified examples; test error for main results, validation error (10% held-out train) for ablations

baselines: Dai and Le 2015 LM fine-tuning (7.64 on IMDb)
eval.protocol: single reported numbers; no seeds, variance or significance test reported; authors note TREC-6 gain is not statistically significant given the 500-example test set. Ablations use unidirectional LMs on IMDb, TREC-6, AG validation sets.

availability.weights: pretrained models open-sourced at same URL

limits: Only text classification on six English datasets is evaluated; sequence labeling is claimed straightforward but not tested, and entailment/QA may need new methods.
Pretraining corpus is only Wikitext-103 (103M words); more diverse corpora left to future work.
No seeds, variance, confidence intervals or compute/hardware are reported; TREC-6 gain is acknowledged as not statistically significant.
Hyperparameters were tuned on the IMDb validation set and reused across tasks; ablations use validation error on 10% of training data, so they are not test results.

Gradual unfreezing and slanted triangular LR were found empirically (e.g. the 2.6 factor); authors say more studies are needed to understand what a pretrained LM captures and how fine-tuning changes it.
Dated: AWD-LSTM base; later transformer LMs superseded it (not in the paper).

terms.definition: Tune each layer with a different learning rate; last-layer LR chosen first, lower layers use eta_(l-1) = eta_l/2.6
Learning rate schedule that first linearly increases then linearly decays, with a short increase and long decay
Unfreeze the model one layer at a time starting from the last layer, fine-tuning all unfrozen layers one epoch per step until all layers are fine-tuned
Concatenate last hidden state with max-pooled and mean-pooled hidden states over as many time steps as fit in GPU memory
BPTT for Text Classification: split document into fixed-length batches, carry state across batches, backpropagate to batches that contributed to the prediction
In NLP, concatenation of embeddings at different layers of a pretrained model used as features

code.snippet: theta_t^l = theta_{t-1}^l - eta^l * grad_{theta^l} J(theta); eta^{l-1} = eta^l / 2.6
cut = floor(T * cut_frac); p = t/cut if t < cut else 1 - (t-cut)/(cut*(ratio-1)); eta_t = eta_max * (1 + p*(ratio-1)) / ratio
